scenario_1_spad_investigation.summary:
**Verdict:** Train 12414 stopped 60 m short of the Home Signal at Danger at Suratgarh. The Station Master confirmed no SPAD. The radio record shows the stop came from the Assistant Loco Pilot's warning about phone use, not from the Loco Pilot's own signal observance.

**What was heard (Railcomm)**
- [03:11:05] Station Master: Down Loop Line set, Home Signal at Danger, Caution Order 30 km/h.
- [03:11:22] ALP repeated the order back (call-out protocol followed).
- [03:13:45] ALP called the Distant Signal at Yellow and asked to reduce speed.
- [03:14:15] ALP: "Put down the phone, Home Signal ahead is RED! Apply brakes!"
- [03:14:24] LP reported emergency brake applied, brake pipe at 0 kg/cm².
- [03:14:48] LP reported a complete halt 60 m before the Home Signal.
- [03:15:10] Station Master: signal not passed, no SPAD. Section Controller informed.

**What was seen (Locate)**
- The cab camera has **no phone alert at the moment of the warning**: records between [03:13:36] and [03:14:40] are routine monitoring, auto-suppressed.
- The same train has 43 confirmed phone alerts this shift, the nearest at [02:46:24] before and [03:44:32] after the incident.

**Assessment:** Phone use is corroborated by the ALP's radio warning and by repeated confirmed cab alerts, but not captured in the incident minute. Pull the CVVRS footage for 03:13–03:15 before any charge: an AI alert alone must not be the basis of action (Railways Act Section 175).

**Rules engaged:** G&SR 3.78 (signal at danger), G&SR 4.40 (calling out signal aspects), G&SR 4.09 (caution orders), Railway Board Safety Circular No. 2018/Safety(A&R)/19/19 (in-cab phones).
